subject.title: fix(gateway): bound connect frame auth.* fields at the protocol schema

question: Should OpenClaw accept the new 256, 2048, and 4096 connect-auth caps as the permanent pre-auth protocol boundary, including fail-closed rejection for outlier shared secrets and overlong local agent runtime identities?
rationale: The code direction is sound, but this is a security-sensitive auth boundary and compatibility tradeoff; automation should not choose the permanent token/password/runtime-token contract without gateway/security owner intent.

options.title: Accept these caps after owner review
options.body: Land the PR if gateway/security owners agree the caps are generous enough and the fail-closed behavior is the desired protocol contract.

options.title: Adjust caps or producer contracts first
options.body: Change the constants or upstream producer/session-key contracts before merge if owners want a different compatibility envelope.

options.title: Narrow to machine-minted bootstrap/device tokens
options.body: Land only the iterated-token DoS mitigation here and leave shared-secret/runtime-token caps for a separate owner-approved protocol decision.

recommendation.title: Accept these caps after owner review
recommendation.body: Land the PR if gateway/security owners agree the caps are generous enough and the fail-closed behavior is the desired protocol contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the gateway protocol package and is the best available owner for the protocol compatibility choice.
